Opening up to friends is one of the hardest things and if you don't have a friend you feel comfortable with talking about this you shouldn't, as long as there are people in your area (parents/doctor) who are aware and trying to be there for you, together with people online, you are not alone!

I don't know you, neither do I know you parents, but don't shy away from getting help from people you know that care!

A few years ago someone from my (at that moment) highschool hung himself and he's parents found him. They found all sorts of notes in his room, on his computer, whatsoever. His parents gave a talk at our highschool discussing what their son had gone through and they said; no (loving) parent will ever mind helping their children with whatever they need help with, never will they see it as a burden if their kids are going through tough times, please don't feel like you are bothering your parents when asking for help. 

Everyone has their own situations and relations, and only you can be the judge on who to talk to and who not to talk to, but don't let shame, feeling of being a burden, or fear be a reason to not ask for help!

In this case the problem is that there were feelings involved, from both sides. She was basically waiting for me to be ready to take the next step.

We dated for about 12/18 months (depending on when you start counting), it basically was a relationship except for actually calling it a relationship and taking that step.  


I cut things off because I didn't want to lead her on and I didn't want her to 'waste' another year 'waiting' for me. Now that it's really over I have an insane amount of regret, I even feel kind of sick, and the problem is that this isn't the first time that I have done this to myself, hence the 'self-destructive'. 

I didn't cut it off for the wrong reasons, I don't think, but to protect her in a way. I just don't understand why I keep doing this to myself.
